blocks.etymology: From Middle English snorten, from earlier fnorten, from Old English *fnorettan, related to Middle English snoren, fnoren, from Old English fnora. See snore and sneeze for more on the change from fn- to sn-.

senses.definition: to make a harsh sound by blowing air forcefully through your nose, often showing anger or amusement

examples.en: She snorted in disbelief when she heard his ridiculous excuse.

examples: The board threw the man out, because he wouldn't cooperate and agree with their plans to remodernize the facility.
